Eve_Corp_SRE: Hey team — we're hitting a barrage of 429s from the embeddings endpoint during our nightly bulk job. Started ~02:10 UTC and spikes every ~5–10 minutes for the last hour. Job details:
- model: rwd-embed-1024 (embedding vector size 1024)
- batch size: 1024 vectors per request (we know it's large but this was our perf win)
- concurrency: 16 worker threads
- total vectors: ~2.1M over 2h window

Errors look like: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 10
{
  "error": {"message":"rate_limit_exceeded","type":"rate_limit", "details":"burst_limit"}
}
```
Sometimes Retry-After is missing and we just get a 429 with no body. We tried exponential backoff but still see steady 429s after ~30–45m. Anyone seen this pattern?

Alice_Support: Thanks @Eve_Corp_SRE — sorry for the interruption. Can you paste one full curl of a failing request (headers + body trimmed if large) and the full response headers when available? Also: which account/org id is this under, and are you on a committed Dedicated plan or hosted pay-as-you-go? That helps with quota windows.

Eve_Corp_SRE: Provided sanitized curl below (we replaced vectors with [...]) and included response headers we captured. Account: org-67321, hosted pay-as-you-go.
```
curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-1024","input":[...1024 vectors...]}'

< HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests\n< Retry-After: 8\n< X-Request-Id: rq_8a3f21\n< Content-Type: application/json\n
{"error":{"message":"rate_limit_exceeded","type":"rate_limit","details":"burst_limit"}}
```
We also see responses where Retry-After is absent and X-Request-Id varies.

Alice_Support: Two parallel things: (1) immediate mitigations you can run client-side, (2) infra checks on our side. For client-side, try these ASAP: reduce concurrency to <=4, reduce batch size to 256 (or 128 if latency still high), and implement exponential backoff with jitter. Example pseudo-retry: 
```
# exponential backoff w/ full jitter (python-ish)
import random, time
def backoff(attempt):
  base = 0.5
  max_sleep = 30
  sleep = min(max_sleep, base * 2**attempt)
  time.sleep(random.random() * sleep)
```
Also check for mixed error classes — dimension mismatch errors (400) will not benefit from backoff.

Sam_Infra: Adding infra notes — we see a recurring burst window throttle on org-67321. Hosted pay-as-you-go has a soft burst limit: sustained throughput allowed but bursts over X RPS in a short window will return 429 with details "burst_limit". We should be able to either (A) temporarily raise your burst cap for the maintenance window or (B) recommend switching to the async/bulk ingestion endpoint that tolerates queued work. @Alice_Support can file a quota request.

Eve_Corp_SRE: Async endpoint? Link? And will switching change billing? We need to preserve ordering and determinism of embeddings (we assign IDs client-side).

Alice_Support: Docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/embeddings/bulk (internal link). Async keeps your per-request payloads smaller and lets our queue absorb bursts; results pushed to an S3-compatible output or polled. Billing is per vector processed; queueing doesn't change per-vector billing but may change peak concurrency and help avoid throttles.

quota-bot: Ticket created: SUP-98765 — quota bump request submitted for org-67321. Current status: pending manual review by infra. ETA: 4–8h.

Maria_Engineer: Quick internal repro notes we added to SUP-98765: we replayed a client load with 16 workers x 1024-vector payloads and observed tokenized throughput spike causing our burst window to trip after ~25–40 minutes; the rate limiter returns 429 w/ no Retry-After in some code paths — that's a bug we're tracking (we should always include Retry-After). Also flagged that some 400-dimension-mismatch errors were surfacing earlier in the logs for other customers — unrelated but noisy.

Eve_Corp_SRE: We switched to concurrency=4 and batch=256 and ran for 90 minutes — no 429s so far. Great. Could you confirm whether those 429s are counted as billable retries? We had ~15k failed requests that retried automatically.

Alice_Support: Good to hear the mitigation worked. 429 responses are not charged for successful output, but the initial failed request still counts as an API request in usage metrics; embeddings are charged per successfully generated vector. We can also grant a one-time goodwill credit for the period if you'd like — I can add that to the ticket.

Sam_Infra: Action items: (1) temporarily increase burst cap for org-67321 until 2026-03-22 23:59 UTC, (2) patch rate limiter to always emit Retry-After header (low-risk change), (3) add async/bulk link to the support KB. I'll coordinate with deployment window.

Alice_Support: @Eve_Corp_SRE I'll keep SUP-98765 open and follow up when infra confirms the cap bump and the Retry-After fix. For longer-term: recommend migrating to the bulk ingestion API for this pattern or consider dedicated capacity (Reserved/Dedicated) if you need predictable heavy nightly throughput.

Eve_Corp_SRE: Thanks everyone — the temporary client changes are a good stopgap. Please proceed with the cap bump and the Retry-After patch. Would appreciate a quick note when the goodwill credit is applied. :thumbsup:

Maria_Engineer: Noted, will follow up on the bug and update the ticket with the fix PR.

Alice_Support: Closing loop: SUP-98765 updated — infra scheduled cap bump + Retry-After patch in next Canary (ETA ~6h). Credit note added, will confirm when applied. If you see regressions after changes, please reopen this thread or ping #incidents. :raised_hands:
